primary_cause: Evidence confirms a recent Capesize freight-rate and demand improvement, but the exact durability and breadth of the dry-bulk commodity-volume cycle are unresolved because BIMCO reporting attributes apparent 2026 strength partly to forced rerouting and warns of a future supply glut.
counter_evidence: BIMCO warned that dry-bulk market strength in 2026 was substantially artificial because of forced rerouting and that a 2027 supply glut could reverse the benefit. source_summary: A key dry-bulk rate measure reached its highest level since December 2023, driven by rising Capesize demand and tightening vessel supply. [Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand] https://gcaptain.com/dry-bulk-shipping-rates-hit-two-year-high-on-capesize-demand/

primary_cause: Recent reporting supports continued storage and memory growth, but the evidence does not establish a time-consistent industry-wide NAND pricing, inventory, and controller/module cycle; available commentary also questions whether historical NAND cyclicality remains applicable.
counter_evidence: Industry commentary argues that NAND supply may not respond to demand through the familiar historical cycle, weakening the inference that current growth represents a conventional NAND cycle. [The Next NAND Decade: Why Supply Can’t Catch Demand The Way It Used To] https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbestechcouncil/2026/05/01/the-next-nand-decade-why-supply-cant-catch-demand-the-way-it-used-to/
source_summary: The 2026 Future of Memory and Storage Conference highlighted continued growth in storage and memory demand, including AI-related storage requirements.
